title: Literature check 2: the Marangoni nematic rods that met C:swim-divide-bd are a variant of Giomi and DeSimone 2014 (active nematic droplets divide and move by their active stress, so the passive twin's failure is expected); Bergmann et al. 2023's fuel-driven liquid shells explain c40's hollowing founder but would not give B
summary: Opened 2 primary abstracts. Giomi and DeSimone 2014 already show spontaneous division and motility of active nematic droplets from their active stress; c34's rods add formation from noise, a self-made surfactant ring with a held, inherited cargo, and a Marangoni back-action that lengthens swimming runs. Bergmann et al. 2023 show chemically fuelled droplets become liquid shells through gradients of short-lived droplet material; this likely explains c40's hollowing founder at weak turnover, but a shell of body material is not an independent layer, so IBED still needs a second species at the interface.

sources.note: active nematic droplets divide spontaneously and move by self-generated flows; the mechanism under c34's rods and the reason the zeta=0 twin fails
fuel-driven droplets form stable liquid shells via gradients of short-lived droplet material; explains hollow CIPS bodies, not a self-made layer

prior_art.note: division and motility from active nematic stress are published; formation from noise, the self-made ring with inherited cargo and the Marangoni-lengthened runs are what c34 adds
